newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian bank approves share split, bond proposal.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian bank approves share split, bond proposal.

text.p: Shareholders of National Societe Generale Bank approved on Thursday a plan to split the shares into 10 to make them more liquid, a bank official said.
The shares, trading on Thursday at about 1,107 pounds ($325) each, are among the largest units on the Cairo stock exchange.
The shareholders, at an extraordinary assembly, also gave the bank clearance to issue floating-rate bonds up to a maximum of 150 million pounds, the official said.
A National Societe Generale executive said last month that the proposal was to issue five-year bonds at a fixed premium above the yield on Egyptian treasury bills.
The average yield on both three-month and six-month T-bills now stands at just below 10 percent.
The bank has not set a timetable for the issue but it could be about the middle of the year, the official said on Thursday.
The French bank Societe Generale has held a majority stake in National Societe Generale since last October.
